value.frequency: ~300 cut-ins/day (one driver's field estimate) ≈ 27/hr ≈ one every ~2 min of driving

VTTI_2022.threshold: cut-in probability rises once following distance > 23.5 m (~77 ft)
VTTI_2022.response: truck often brakes and re-opens gap by ~15.5 m
VTTI_2022.rate_floor: ~1 close cut-in per ~114 mi — close cases only, so a floor, not the full rate

buffer_vs_threshold.FMCSA_guidance: 1 s per 10 ft of vehicle length + 1 s above 40 mph ≈ 8 s for a 70+ ft rig (from memory, unverified here)
buffer_vs_threshold.result: any safe buffer sits far past the cut-in threshold — the gap that keeps you safe is the gap that invites cut-ins

value.undercount: research counts close cut-ins (~0.8 s) only; every entry into 3-8 s buffer is driver workload, uncounted

false_denominator.instance: automated systems studied on fixed lanes, good weather, close-cut-in metrics, outcome-based judging; humans held to full following-distance rules, HOS, CSA, all weather
false_denominator.fix: same rules, same conditions, same metrics on both sides before comparing
